contracts.commit_point: self.service.events().insert(calendarId=calendar_id, body=event).execute() inside GoogleCalendarService.create_event (lines 122-125) — the executed Google Calendar API insert request that persists the event.
contracts.declared_mechanism: In-tool fail-closed precondition guard: book_appointment calls calendar_service.check_availability(start_dt, end_dt) and, if the check fails, returns 'Cannot book appointment: Time slot is no longer available' before create_event is reached (lines 229-231). check_availability queries events().list over [start_time, end_time] with singleEvents=True on the configured calendarId and returns True only when the returned items list is empty (lines 84-98), returning False on any exception (lines 100-102).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Committing the events().insert(...).execute() write for a slot in which check_availability detected conflicting events (non-empty items list at lines 97-98), i.e., double-booking an occupied time window. The guard as written also prohibits booking whenever the precondition does not pass, because check_availability returns False on any exception (lines 100-102).

contracts.protection_obligation: The book_appointment agent tool must not create a Google Calendar event for a time slot that already contains a conflicting event: calendar_service.check_availability must pass (return True, i.e., no conflicting events found on the configured calendar) before calendar_service.create_event commits the events().insert write to the configured Google Calendar. This consolidates both reviewer phrasings (phase-one 'refuse create_event when check_availability reports a conflict' and phase-two 'check must pass before create_event commits the insert') into one obligation, since both name the same forbidden condition, guard, and commit point.
scope_limits: The check-then-insert sequence is not atomic: no lock, transaction, or optimistic-concurrency control spans check_availability (line 230) and create_event (line 234), so concurrent bookings can still double-book; the obligation covers only the sequential precondition.

The guard exists only inside book_appointment; create_event itself performs no availability check, so any other caller of create_event would be unguarded (no other callers of create_event appear in the supplied source besides book_appointment).
The obligation is bound to the calendarId returned by get_calendar_id() (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID, default 'primary'); bookings against other calendars are outside the stated guard.

Because check_availability returns False on exception (lines 100-102), the guard also blocks booking on Calendar API errors; the obligation as stated prohibits booking whenever the check does not affirmatively pass.
